  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md`, step 2 sync paragraph (line 19) and step 7a `kind=conflict` (line 58)
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff for `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` adds the AD-7 no-sync rule but does not include the AD-10 after-the-gates conflict abort rule or the step 7a final-PR `kind=conflict` pointer that the `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` twin carries at lines 19 and 58. The `.claude/` copy in the working tree confirms this: line 19 ends with "a clean merge is pushed the same way; an up-to-date branch needs no push" (no "After the gates" paragraph), and step 7a at line 58 says "The push starts the next review round." (no "On the final PR (step 11a) the merge brings the base into the project branch after the gates" pointer). The PR description Twin-first section documents the hold and the `test_template_parity` red state as intentional; the hold claim (`ai:claude-fix-claim:v1 head=6113a9093235 kind=hold`) prevents any stage session from exercising the stale `.claude/` copy during the hold window. The gap closes when the `[claude-twin-sync]` copy lands.
  SEVERITY: NIT

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The pass-1 cross-pollination consensus finding flags that a clean base sync after the gates can advance the final PR to a tree not covered by the recorded security or runtime-validation stages, yet step 11a can mark that PR ready without rerunning them
  Expected change site: `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` step 2, lines 19; step 11a, line 86
  Evidence of absence: This is not a gap but an accepted design choice. The plan's Risks section (line 97-100 of the plan) documents: "Residual: a merge in the seconds between step 9's re-check and step 10's dispatch is validated but not re-audited → ACCEPTED, as the chain's own PRs never merge while a read-result stage runs." The step 2 after-the-gates rule at line 19 of the twin says: "A clean merge is pushed the same way, after the gates too (it adds only default-branch commits, which a branch audit's merge-base range excludes)." A clean merge after the gates adds only default-branch commits to the project branch, and those commits fall outside the branch audit's merge-base range (the audit scopes to `merge-base(default, project-branch)..project-branch`). Code authored on the project branch is already audited; default-branch code arriving through a clean sync was already reviewed on its way to default. This is AD-10's deliberate arch: conflict resolution changes project code, clean sync does not.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
